clue.text: What Antony asked of his friends, the theatregoers

definitions.text: What Antony asked of his friends
definitions.meaning: Mark Antony's speech opens 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears': he asked them for a hearing
the people gathered in a theatre to watch a play

explanation.surface: A quiz question about Mark Antony's famous speech, then a nod to the people watching Julius Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Antony begins 'lend me your ears', asking the crowd to listen to him.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a formal hearing granted to a speaker; the other is the assembled spectators at a performance.

clue.text: Jack's over 9, anyhow, that's clear

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, an AB (able seaman); with the 's that gives AB'S

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 9 across, O dear!

explanation.surface: A sailor finds that, whatever happens, the matter is cleared up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' jumbles LOVE (the answer to 9 across) to OLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to clear them of guilt or blame.

clue.text: Feet perhaps standing in Hell

indicators.note: the posture word goes in the middle of the underworld's name

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, and Dante's city of Hell
a stance is a way of standing

explanation.surface: Someone's feet, perhaps, while standing in Hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. Dis was the Roman god of the underworld, and Dante named his city of Hell after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengths measured in feet are examples of measured spans between points.

clue.text: Prince makes one cross

definitions.meaning: the German princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor held this title
a voter marks one X on the ballot paper

explanation.surface: A prince who manages to annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry', but it is the X marked on a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain German princes chose the emperor, and anyone who votes marks a ballot paper.

clue.text: Flier's jacket lieutenant and I wear

indicators.note: the outer garment is worn by the officer and me, so it wraps around them

parts.note: a coat is a jacket

explanation.surface: An airman's jacket, worn by the lieutenant and by me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear' is the container signal: the jacket is what the officer and I wear. 'Flier's' means 'Flier is', so the definition is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This small black-capped bird of the tit family is a flier.

clue.text: This month is about second deepest

indicators.note: the letters for this month go around the letters for second, so they sit inside it

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of the current month in old business letters
mo is a short moment, a second ('half a mo')

explanation.surface: A remark that something this month concerns a second, profound matter.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant, this month) goes about MO (a moment): IN(MO)ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Innermost and inmost both describe the most central, profound part of something.

clue.text: Repeating it before imbibing at tea-time

indicators.note: the word for before drinks in, so contains, the later pieces

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
four o'clock is traditional tea-time, and four is IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A habit of repeating it before having a drink at tea-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibing' is the container signal. Four o'clock is traditional British tea-time, hence the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterative processes are ones carried out again and again.

clue.text: Soldiers point guns upwards one fired inwards.

indicators.note: the later pieces are fired inwards, ending up inside the turned word
in a down clue, upwards means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to point guns at a target is to aim
I is the Roman numeral one
lit means set on fire

explanation.surface: Soldiers point their guns upwards, and one fires inwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwards' turns the word for point guns into MIA in this down clue, and 'inwards' sends one and fired inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a body of citizen soldiers raised in an emergency.

clue.text: Reveals changes in a small number

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the word are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reveals a few changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges REVEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, a small number.

clue.text: Sue at length with X in case A's withdrawn support

indicators.note: the Roman ten is placed in the middle of the longer form of the girl's name

parts.note: Sue is a short form of the name Susan, so Sue given at full length is Susan
X is ten in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the letters A and S are taken away from the word case, leaving its remainder

parts.note: A's gives the letters A and S

explanation.surface: A lawyer drags out a suit against someone called X, in case support is withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts X inside the full name; 'withdrawn' takes A and S out of case, leaving CE to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustenance is food and nourishment that keeps a person going, a form of support.

clue.text: O dear!

definitions.meaning: a nought, the score of nothing in tennis
a term of endearment for a ... one

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay, 'Oh dear!'
explanation.definitionFit: Zero in tennis is called by this word, and a sweetheart is addressed with it too.

clue.text: Mate has to be first with rum to cure a sailor

parts.note: to lead is to be in front, first in the race
a tot is a small measure of spirits, the sailor's traditional rum ration
to heal is to cure
tar, an old word for a sailor (from tarpaulin)

explanation.surface: A ship's mate insists on first giving rum to cure an ailing sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a ship's officer, but it is the verb to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a partner up the aisle of a church means marrying them, and to mate is to pair up.

clue.text: Passage leading right into bar

indicators.note: the opening letter is placed inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar means except, as in 'all bar one'

indicators.note: only the leading, first letter of the word right is used

explanation.surface: A passage that leads right into a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the first letter of 'right', goes into EXCEPT ('bar' as in 'all bar one').
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract quoted from a book or piece of music.

clue.text: The way Simon holds the scenery up

indicators.note: the character's surname holds the turned scenery word inside it

parts.note: Simon Pure is a character in an 18th-century comedy, giving the phrase 'the real Simon Pure'

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: decor is stage scenery

explanation.surface: How Simon holds up the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the scenery word to ROCED in this down clue, and 'holds' puts it inside. 'The real Simon Pure' means the genuine article.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is the established method or way of doing something.

clue.text: Wonder if vehicle's reversing in the distance

indicators.note: the turned-round vehicle goes within the length of road

parts.note: a mile is a measure of distance

indicators.note: the vehicle is reversing, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: It would be a wonder if a car were reversing far off in the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns the vehicle to RAC, and 'in' places it inside the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is an extraordinary event that causes wonder.

clue.text: Alliance of 4 with one, on missing, the end of it'

indicators.note: the bird's name is missing a letter, which is taken out of it

parts.note: the answer to 4 down, the flier

indicators.note: only the end, last letter of the word it is used

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A partnership of four with one more joining, minus the end of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, the end of 'it', from COALTIT (4 down) to get COALIT, then add I and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalition is a union of parties or groups, an alliance.

clue.text: Garland can be made of stone

indicators.note: the letters of the two words can be made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a decorative garland can be carved out of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made' rearranges OF STONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A festoon is a chain of flowers or ribbon hung in a curve, a type of garland.

clue.text: Warning from former liberal

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
liberal means generous, ample

explanation.surface: A warning delivered by a one-time Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' looks political, but it means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Punishing one person as an example serves as a warning to others.

clue.text: Colossal, it makes bird panic, losing head

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: the word panic loses its head, its first letter

explanation.surface: Something enormous makes a little bird panic.
explanation.walkthrough: PANIC losing its head, P, gives ANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, like the Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Forward, the Scots' Own ! You have to belong

parts.note: forward means cheeky, pert
ain is the Scots word for own ('my ain folk')

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to a Scottish regiment, 'Forward, the Scots' Own!', followed by a call to join up.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain is to be attached or relevant to something, to belong to it.

clue.text: Condition if one's caught by an Irish terrorist.

indicators.note: the letters for one's are caught, held inside, the terrorist word

parts.note: a Provo is a member of the Provisional IRA
one's means one is, I plus S

explanation.surface: A condition: if one is captured by an Irish terrorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' is the container signal. Provo was the common name for a member of the Provisional IRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a clause stating a condition in an agreement.

clue.text: One who burgled a famous hotel

definitions.meaning: A. J. ... was E. W. Hornung's gentleman cat burglar
the colonial-era hotel in Singapore where the Singapore Sling was invented

explanation.surface: Someone who broke into a famous hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a fictional gentleman thief and to Singapore's grand colonial hotel.

clue.text: Sniff brightly-coloured flowers

parts.note: to nose is to sniff about
gay in its older sense means bright and colourful

explanation.surface: An instruction to smell some vivid blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' is the definition, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small posy of sweet-smelling flowers.

clue.text: How a rook moves

parts.note: a rook is a crow that flies straight, and the chess rook also moves only in straight lines

explanation.surface: A chess question about how the castle travels across the board.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in a straight line, the direct path a crow takes in flight.

clue.text: Bridge tips the wrong way. .

indicators.note: the word is set down the wrong way round, back to front

parts.note: a nap is a racing tipster's most confident tip

explanation.surface: A bridge that tilts the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPS ('tips', from horse racing) reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the arch or stretch of a bridge between supports, and also the verb to bridge.

clue.text: Stiff as Matthew's withered fig-tree

definitions.meaning: in Matthew 21 Jesus curses a fig tree that bears no fruit and it withers

explanation.surface: A comparison of something rigid with the barren fig tree in St Matthew's Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflexible things refuse to bend, and a tree giving no fruit produces no crop.

clue.text: Make secure

indicators.note: make here invites remaking the letters of the following word into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A simple instruction to make something safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' rearranges SECURE, and the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone from danger is to bring them to safety, making them secure.

clue.text: Relatively given to kissing …

parts.note: kissing cousins are relatives close enough to greet each other with a kiss, so the clue describes behaving like a relative

explanation.surface: A hint of someone fairly fond of kissing.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means in the manner of a family member of the next generation sideways, as with kissing cousins.
